mainTopic: Who receives the קנס for a נערה: the readings of בתולה and אשר לא אורסה, the two versions of רבי עקיבא, and a girl who died
overview: The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא uses the words בתולה and אשר לא אורסה in the קנס פסוקים. After some back-and-forth, it concludes that בתולה excludes a בעולה, because her body changed. אשר לא אורסה is then used for the גזירה שוה between אונס and מפתה, so a divorced ארוסה still gets a קנס. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the same comparison from the phrase כמוהר הבתולות instead. Next, the גמרא notes that רבי עקיבא's view is reported two ways: the fine goes to the girl or to her father. It answers that two תנאים reported his view differently. רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ברייתא's version by reading the words as 'who is not betrothed now.' רבה follows the משנה's version instead. רב חסדא then explains a ברייתא's dispute over who gets the fine as this same split. Finally, אביי rules there is no קנס if the girl died, while רבא asks whether a dead girl can become a בוגרת in the grave, so that the fine would go to her son rather than her father.

steps.title: Why not flip the two words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reversing רבי עקיבא's reading. Let בתולה be used for the גזירה שוה, and let אשר לא אורסה exclude a girl who was betrothed and divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the opposite: the word בתולה is for the גזירה שוה, and the words אשר לא אורסה come to exclude a נערה who was betrothed and then divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way it just explained רבי עקיבא. It asks why the two words could not swap jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אשר לא אורסה was used for the גזירה שוה between אונס and מפתה, and בתולה excluded a בעולה. Both words appear in both פסוקים, so either one could serve as the link. If the words swapped jobs, אשר לא אורסה would exclude the divorced ארוסה, which is רבי יוסי הגלילי's view and not רבי עקיבא's.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a suggestion to read it differently)
A teaching that links two passages through a shared word
A young girl who was betrothed and then divorced

phrases.english: Say: "virgin" is for a verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: The word appears in both the rape and seduction פסוקים (דברים 22:28, שמות 22:15).

phrases.english: and "who was not betrothed"
comes to exclude a young woman who was betrothed and divorced!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation of how רבי עקיבא divides the two words
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of אשר לא אורסה to the גזירה שוה and בתולה to the exclusion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both words are shared by the two פסוקים, so nothing forces this assignment. The reverse is just as possible.

steps.title: She is still a נערה בתולה
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to use אשר לא אורסה for the גזירה שוה. A divorced ארוסה is still a נערה בתולה, so the פסוק still describes her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical that אשר לא אורסה is for the גזירה שוה, because I can still call her a נערה בתולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the original reading. The divorced girl still fits the main description in the פסוק, which is נערה בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she is still a virgin girl, it seems wrong to exclude her just because of the extra words אשר לא אורסה. So those words are better used for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because I can still apply this description to her

phrases.english: It stands to reason that "who was not betrothed" is for the verbal analogy,
since I can still call her "a young woman who is a virgin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by defending the original division
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either word could be the one that excludes
steps.terutzMaskana: The divorced ארוסה still fits נערה בתולה, so she should not be excluded

steps.title: The argument works the other way too
steps.stepSummary: The same logic can be turned around. A בעולה can still be described as אשר לא אורסה, so maybe בתולה is the word for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: use בתולה for the גזירה שוה, since I can still describe her as אשר לא אורסה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a mirror-image argument against the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl who is not a virgin but was never betrothed still fits אשר לא אורסה. So the argument 'she still fits the other description' does not settle which word should do the excluding.

phrases.english: On the contrary: "virgin" is for the verbal analogy,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אֲנִי קוֹרֵא בָּהּ ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא אוֹרָסָה״!
phrases.english: since I can still describe her as "who was not betrothed"!
phrases.notes: Here 'her' is a girl who is no longer a virgin but was never betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer's own reasoning against it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reasoning is symmetrical, so it cannot decide which word is the one that excludes.

steps.title: Her body changed, and the other's did not
steps.stepSummary: The deciding difference is physical. A בעולה has changed physically, but a divorced ארוסה has not, so it makes sense that only the בעולה loses the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason: this one (the בעולה) has a changed body, and that one (the divorced ארוסה) does not have a changed body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason that breaks the tie. Losing virginity is a real physical change, but a betrothal and divorce are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the בעולה is physically different, it is logical that the word בתולה excludes her. The divorced ארוסה is physically the same as before, so she keeps her קנס. That means אשר לא אורסה is free for the גזירה שוה, which supports רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, בתולה excludes a בעולה, because her body changed. אשר לא אורסה is used for the גזירה שוה, so a divorced ארוסה still gets a קנס.

phrases.english: It stands to reason: this one, her body changed,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the girl who is no longer a virgin; 'that one', in the next line, is the girl who was betrothed and divorced.

phrases.english: and that one, her body did not change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock from step 3
steps.terutzMaskana: A physical change is a stronger reason to exclude, so בתולה is the word that excludes

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי get the comparison?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי uses אשר לא אורסה to exclude the divorced ארוסה. So where does he learn the shared rules of אונס and מפתה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי, where does he get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי הגלילי. It asks for his source for the comparison between אונס and מפתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learned the comparison from אשר לא אורסה. For אונס that means fifty and the same amount for מפתה, and for מפתה that means שקלים and the same coin for אונס. רבי יוסי הגלילי has already used those words to exclude the divorced ארוסה, so he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: Where does he learn it from?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַאי סְבָרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, from where does he derive this conclusion?
phrases.notes: 'This conclusion' means that the amount and the type of coin are the same for rape and seduction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַאי סְבָרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי עקיבא's source is settled, it asks for רבי יוסי הגלילי's source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source for linking the rules of אונס and מפתה

steps.title: Learned from מוהר הבתולות
steps.stepSummary: He learns it from a ברייתא on the phrase כסף ישקול כמוהר הבתולות. The two fines are compared in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a ברייתא: 'He shall weigh money like the מוהר of the virgins.' This one is like the מוהר הבתולות, and the מוהר הבתולות is like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's source: a ברייתא that reads the phrase מוהר הבתולות as a two-way comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine for מפתה is set equal to the fine for אונס, which is fifty. The fine for אונס is set equal to the fine for מפתה, which is paid in שקלים. So רבי יוסי הגלילי does not need אשר לא אורסה for this.

keyTerms.meaning: From what was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both תנאים agree about the amount and the coin of the fine. They disagree only about which פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: He derives it from what was taught:
"He shall weigh money like the dowry of the virgins,"
that this should be like the dowry of the virgins,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the seduction fine, which becomes fifty like the rape fine.

phrases.english: and the dowry of the virgins should be like this.
phrases.notes: So the rape fine is paid in שקלים, like the seduction fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A two-way comparison learned from כמוהר הבתולות

steps.title: רבי עקיבא contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא says the fine for a divorced ארוסה goes to her. In the ברייתא, he says it goes to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: רבי עקיבא contradicts רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two statements of רבי עקיבא conflict with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources agree with רבי עקיבא that a divorced ארוסה does get a קנס. The problem is who receives it: in the משנה it goes to herself, and in the ברייתא it goes to her father.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: The משנה says the fine goes to her, and the ברייתא says it goes to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new issue about רבי עקיבא's consistency
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling about who receives the fine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה and the ברייתא quote him with opposite rulings on who gets the money.

steps.title: Two reports of רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: Two תנאים reported רבי עקיבא's opinion differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are two תנאים, each reporting the view of רבי עקיבא differently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא himself did not contradict himself. Two later תנאים passed down his view in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reconciling the two sources, the גמרא says each one reflects a different report of what רבי עקיבא held. Both reports still agree that she gets a קנס.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי עקיבא changed his mind. It means two students reported his opinion differently.

phrases.english: These are two tanna'im, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the same תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים reported רבי עקיבא's view differently

steps.title: Does the ברייתא's version of רבי עקיבא erase the verse's plain meaning?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's רבי עקיבא keeps the plain meaning of אשר לא ארשה. The ברייתא's רבי עקיבא seems to let the גזירה שוה wipe it out completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי עקיבא of the משנה: a גזירה שוה does not push a verse entirely away from its simple meaning. But according to רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא, does a גזירה שוה really push the verse entirely away from its simple meaning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a problem on the version of רבי עקיבא found in the ברייתא. In that version, the phrase אשר לא ארשה seems to have no meaning left at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of אשר לא ארשה is that a girl who was once betrothed is treated differently: her fine goes to her and not to her father. רבי עקיבא of the משנה keeps that difference. רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא gives the fine to the father in every case, so the words אשר לא ארשה serve only the גזירה שוה (Steps 1-4). That would leave the words with no simple meaning at all, which is normally not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this one is fine, but that one is hard' question)
A teaching that links two passages through a shared word or phrase
The simple, plain meaning of the verse

steps.confusionAlert: The rule is not that a גזירה שוה can never add to a verse. The rule is that it cannot wipe out the verse's plain meaning COMPLETELY.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a general rule of reading the Torah: no teaching may erase a verse's simple meaning entirely.

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Akiva of the Mishnah:
a verbal analogy does not come
and take the verse entirely out of its plain meaning.
phrases.notes: For him, 'who was not betrothed' still means what it says: a girl who was once betrothed gets the fine herself.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Akiva of the Baraita,
does a verbal analogy come
and take it entirely out of its plain meaning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the two versions of רבי עקיבא from Step 8 and challenges the ברייתא's version.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fine always goes to the father, then אשר לא ארשה has no plain meaning left. A גזירה שוה is not allowed to do that.

steps.title: Read the verse as 'who is not betrothed'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the phrase as describing the girl's present status: she is not betrothed right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Read it as 'who is not betrothed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ברייתא's version of רבי עקיבא. He gives the phrase a plain meaning that still works for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'who was never betrothed,' the words mean 'who is not betrothed now.' The phrase then simply excludes a girl who is currently betrothed. It says nothing about a girl who was betrothed and divorced, so her fine can still go to the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as (a new way of reading the words)
A betrothed girl (after אירוסין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Read it as: "who is not betrothed."
phrases.notes: The written word אֹרָשָׂה sounds like 'was betrothed.' He reads it as describing her status right now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase means 'never betrothed,' so the ברייתא's version erases it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means 'not betrothed now.' It keeps a plain meaning, and the fine for a divorced ארוסה can still go to the father.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed for a betrothed girl?
steps.stepSummary: Violating a betrothed girl is punished by stoning, so of course no fine is paid. Why would the verse need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A betrothed girl is a case of stoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's new reading. It seems to teach something we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One who violates a betrothed girl is put to death by stoning. A person who gets the death penalty does not also pay money. So excluding a currently betrothed girl from the fine seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: A betrothed girl is a case of stoning!
phrases.notes: The man gets the death penalty, and someone who gets the death penalty does not also pay money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading 'who is not betrothed'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Death penalty already cancels money payments, so the verse would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: Without the verse, we might think the fine is paid even with death
steps.stepSummary: The fine is a special Torah rule, so we might have thought it is paid even when the man is executed. The verse teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the fine is a new rule the Torah made, he pays it even though he is killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the verse is still needed. We might have treated the fine as an exception to the usual rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, death and money payment do not go together. But the קנס is an unusual Torah rule, a payment beyond normal damages. So we might have thought it is paid even alongside the death penalty. The verse removes that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say
A new, unusual rule that does not follow normal logic
A fixed fine set by the Torah

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since it is a novelty
that the Torah introduced with the fine,
even though he is killed, he pays.
phrases.notes: The verse is needed to show this is wrong: when he is executed, there is no fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the קנס is a special rule, it is paid even together with the death penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that the קנס is not paid when the man is executed.

steps.title: What about רבה, who holds the fine is paid even with death?
steps.stepSummary: רבה really does hold that the fine is paid even when the man is executed. So for him, what does the phrase teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבה, who said that the fine is a new rule the Torah made, so he pays even though he is killed, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבה actually holds the view the verse was just said to reject. For him, the answer in Step 12 does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the verse is needed to reject the idea that the fine is paid even with death. But רבה accepts that idea as the law. So for רבה, the phrase cannot be teaching that, and the question is what it does teach.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who holds the קנס is paid even when the man is executed
What is there to say? (how can this be answered?)

phrases.english: And according to Rabba, who said:
it is a novelty that the Torah introduced with the fine,
so even though he is killed, he pays —
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 12 cannot work for רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: How רבה can explain אשר לא ארשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה holds the very view that, according to Step 12, the verse was written to reject.

steps.title: רבה follows the משנה's version of רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה reads the verse like רבי עקיבא of the משנה: it is about a girl who was betrothed and then divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי עקיבא of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה does not need רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading at all. He uses the plain reading of רבי עקיבא in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, אשר לא ארשה means 'who was never betrothed,' just as the words say. It teaches that a girl who was betrothed and divorced gets her fine herself. So the verse is not about a currently betrothed girl, and רבה's view about death and the fine causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (follows the opinion of)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of אשר לא ארשה. רבי עקיבא of the משנה (and רבה): a divorced ארוסה, whose fine goes to her. רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא (as explained by רב נחמן בר יצחק): a girl who is betrothed right now.

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Akiva of the Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the אמורא within one side of an existing dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה must read the verse as being about a currently betrothed girl.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה reads it like the משנה's רבי עקיבא, as being about a divorced ארוסה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: does the fine go to the father or to the girl?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records two views: the fine goes to her father, or the fine goes to the girl herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: To whom does her fine go? To her father. Some say: to herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a disagreement about who receives the קנס. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view matches the פסוק, which says the man pays the girl's father. The second view, that the girl gets the money herself, sounds surprising. It needs explaining.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Her fine, to whom is it paid? To her father.
And some say: to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source on the same topic of who receives the fine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: the fine goes to the father, or to the girl herself.

steps.title: Why would the fine go to her?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק clearly says the fine goes to the father. How can anyone say it goes to the girl?
steps.simpleTranslation: To herself? Why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second view in the ברייתא, because it seems to go against the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the man gives fifty silver pieces to the girl's father. So the view that the fine goes to the girl seems to contradict an explicit verse.

phrases.english: To herself? Why?
phrases.notes: דברים 22:29 says the man pays the girl's father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second opinion of the ברייתא in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The יש אומרים in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly gives the fine to the father.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the ברייתא is about a divorced ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a girl who was betrothed and divorced. Its two views match the two versions of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Here we are dealing with a נערה who was betrothed and then divorced. They disagree the same way רבי עקיבא of the משנה and רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא is about one special case, a divorced ארוסה. Its dispute is the same split we already saw between the two versions of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a girl who was never betrothed, everyone agrees the fine goes to the father. For a divorced ארוסה, the first view follows the ברייתא's רבי עקיבא (to the father). The יש אומרים follows the משנה's רבי עקיבא (to herself). So the יש אומרים does not go against the פסוק. It speaks about the special case that אשר לא ארשה sets apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with (narrows the case)
She was betrothed and then divorced

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's dispute (father or herself) is only about a divorced ארוסה. It is the same dispute as the two versions of רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Here we are dealing with a young woman who was betrothed and divorced,
and they disagree in the dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּבָרַיְיתָא.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Akiva of the Mishnah and Rabbi Akiva of the Baraita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) and linking it to an existing dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יש אומרים gives every girl's fine to herself, against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is only about a divorced ארוסה, and it matches the two versions of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: אביי: no fine if the girl died
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that if the girl died, the man is exempt from the קנס, based on the wording 'the father of the נערה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If a man was with a girl and then she died, he does not pay the fine. The פסוק says 'he shall give to the father of the girl.' That means a living girl, not the father of a dead girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from אביי: if the girl dies, the man does not pay the קנס at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads the word 'הנערה' closely. The פסוק pictures a girl who is still alive. Once she has died, her father is the father of a dead girl, not 'the father of the נערה', so the payment falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine the Torah sets, here 50 silver pieces
Exempt; he does not have to pay
A young girl between about 12 and 12½

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If he had relations with her, and she died,
he is exempt,
as it is stated: "And he shall give to the father of the girl"
and not to the father of a dead girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the קנס: what happens if the girl dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the girl dies, the man is exempt from the קנס, because the פסוק speaks of 'the father of the נערה' and not the father of a dead girl.

steps.title: What was obvious to אביי was a question for רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's ruling was not obvious to רבא, and sets up רבא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that was simple and clear to אביי was a real question for רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to show רבא's question, which proves he was unsure about what אביי found obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי was sure that a dead girl's father gets nothing. רבא was not so sure that the payment just disappears. The next step shows how.

keyTerms.meaning: It was a question, it was unclear

phrases.english: A matter that was obvious to Abaye
was a question for Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְאַבָּיֵי מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares אביי's clear ruling with רבא's doubt, as a lead-in to רבא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's ruling about a dead girl was not obvious to רבא.

steps.title: רבא asks: can a girl become grown in the grave?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a girl who died can count as having become a בוגרת after death. If so, the קנס goes to her son. If not, it goes to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Does a girl 'grow up' in the grave or not? If she does grow up in the grave, the fine belongs to her son. Or maybe she does not grow up in the grave, and the fine belongs to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a real question, a בעיא, about who gets the קנס when the girl has died: her son or her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question assumes the קנס is still owed after she dies. That is exactly what אביי said is not so. The only doubt for רבא is who receives it: if time counts her as a בוגרת even after death, the money is hers and passes to her son as her heir; if not, she stays a נערה and it goes to her father.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming a בּוֹגֶרֶת, a fully grown woman (from 12½)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about whether there is a fine. His question takes for granted that the fine is paid. He only asks who gets it. That is why the גמרא says this was not obvious to רבא the way it was to אביי.

phrases.english: As Rava asked:
Is there becoming grown in the grave,
phrases.notes: He means: she died a נערה, but by now she would have been 12½ if she had lived.

phrases.english: or is there no becoming grown in the grave?
Is there becoming grown in the grave,
and so it belongs to her son,
or perhaps there is no becoming grown in the grave,
and so it belongs to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the question that proves the matter was not obvious to רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a girl dies as a נערה but would now be a בוגרת, does she count as grown after death, so that the קנס goes to her son, or does it go to her father?
